title: How to build savings for irregular annual bills like property taxes or HOA fees
description: Creating a personal escrow system to manage large, lumpy housing expenses.
content:
For homeowners, the monthly mortgage payment is just the tip of the iceberg. The real budget-killers are the large, irregular bills that hit once or twice a year: Property Taxes, Homeowners Association (HOA) dues, and Insurance premiums. If you don't have an escrow account with your lender (or if you paid off your house), these bills can range from $3,000 to $15,000 annually. Treating them as 'emergencies' is a failure of planning. This guide explains how to smooth out these lumps by building a personal escrow system.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Personal Escrow' Concept: Divide your total annual tax/HOA liability by 12. Transfer that amount monthly to a dedicated savings account. When the bill comes, the money is there.
  • Yield Arbitrage: By holding this cash in a High-Yield Savings Account (earning ~4-5%) instead of letting the bank hold it in a 0% escrow, you earn hundreds of dollars in interest annually.
  • Assessment Shock: Property taxes often jump after a home sale or reassessment. Always budget 10% higher than last year's bill to absorb the increase.
  • The HOA Trap: HOAs can issue 'Special Assessments' for unexpected repairs (e.g., a new roof for the condo building). You need a specific buffer for this beyond regular dues.

Why It Matters (US Context)

In the US, property taxes fund local schools and vary wildly by state. New Jersey has an effective rate of ~2.2%, while Hawaii is ~0.3%. Understanding your local tax cycle (e.g., bills due in Nov and April) is critical for cash flow management.

The Escrow Math

Let's assume you own a home in a state like Texas (high property tax) with an HOA.

The Annual Liability

  • Property Taxes: $8,000 (Due Jan 31).
  • HOA Dues: $1,200 (Due Mar 1).
  • Home Insurance: $1,800 (Due May 1).
  • Total: $11,000 / year.

The Monthly Sinking Fund

$11,000 / 12 = $916/month.

You must treat this $916 as a mandatory bill, just like electricity. If you don't save it monthly, you will be scrambling for $8,000 in January.

Why DIY Escrow Wins

If you pay your mortgage lender to handle escrow, that $11,000 sits in their account earning them interest. If you handle it yourself, that $11,000 sits in your HYSA earning 4.5%. That is ~$500/year in free money just for paying your own bills.

Execution Steps

  1. Open 'The Vault': Create a specific sub-account in your bank named 'Taxes and HOA'. Do not mix this with your Emergency Fund.
  2. Automate the Transfer: Set up an auto-draft of $916 (from the example) on the 1st of every month. Treat it like the mortgage payment.
  3. Calendar Alerts: Set reminders 30 days before the bills are due. 'Transfer from Vault to Checking'.
  4. The Assessment Buffer: If your local government reassesses homes every 3 years, increase your savings rate by 15% in the reassessment year to cover the likely hike.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I pay property taxes with a credit card?

Yes, but there is usually a 2.5% fee. Only do this if you are earning a 'Sign Up Bonus' worth more than the fee. Otherwise, pay by e-check (free).

What is a Special Assessment?

A surprise bill from an HOA for major repairs. If the condo reserve fund is low, they bill owners. Keep an extra $2,000 buffer for this.

Can I invest this money?

No. The timeline is <1 year. Keep it in cash (HYSA or Money Market). You cannot risk the stock market dropping 20% the week your taxes are due.
